title: Who's Who: Ibrahim Sayegh
summary: Physician and optical investigator whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Ibrahim Sayegh (1769–1835) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a physician and optical investigator whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.
Working with surgical mirrors and darkened examination rooms, Sayegh documented the interference lull in 1806. His methods made faint residuals visible without extravagant apparatus.
He also cautioned against exposing patients to experimental openings, a warning ignored by several of his admirers.

For Alderwick readers, Ibrahim Sayegh is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
